claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria was a Christian theologian and head of the Catechetical School of Alexandria, born around 185 CE in Alexandria and dying around 254 CE in Tyre.
The work known as “Notes on Joshua” consists of Origen’s homilies on the biblical book of Joshua, delivered shortly before his torture and death during the Decian persecution, around 254 CE.
Origen addressed these homilies to his Christian hearers, using the story of Israel’s conquest as an allegory for the Christian life from baptism to resurrection.
The original Greek texts of the homilies have been lost; the work survives only in a Latin translation made by Rufinus of Aquileia (c. 345–410).
The Latin translation by Rufinus is the basis for modern English editions, such as the CUA Press translation.
The homilies were composed in the context of the Decian persecution, a period of empire‑wide oppression of Christians that led to Origen’s torture and eventual death.
Origen’s interpretation of Joshua is significant because he re‑reads the violent conquest narratives apocalyptically, presenting the cross of Christ as the means of overcoming evil without violence.
A 9th‑century manuscript from Lorsch, Germany preserves Rufinus’s Latin translation of Origen’s Homilies on Joshua.
